validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: strongly confirmed independent of GEM. Egypt's Ministry of Petroleum (petroleum.gov.eg, Dec-2022 year-end report) names 'خط التينة غرب / ميت نما / الشرقاوية' (El Tina West/Mit Nema/Al-Sharqawiya line), 168 km, completed during 2022. Youm7 (2 May 2022) quotes the Petroleum Minister naming GASCO's implementation of 'خط غاز التينة غرب / ميت نما بطول 170 كم' (170 km) at an announced cost of EGP 4.5bn, purpose = carrying East Mediterranean field gas (Zohr/Nooros-era) toward Cairo/South Valley. Egypt Oil & Gas (English, 3 May 2022) independently reports the same EGP-4.5bn El-Tina/Mit Nema line taking East Med gas to Cairo/South Valley. Masrawy (4 Mar 2024) reports completion of the 'final phase' of 'خط غاز التينة غرب - ميت نما' at 167 km during 2023. Youm7 (14 Jan 2024, current sheet ref) confirms 'تشغيل ازدواج خط التينة غرب/ميت نما' (operation of the El Tina West/Mit Nema duplication/twin line), 168 km, 42-inch, ~EGP 4bn, i.e. a capacity-doubling second pipe on the same corridor, completed 2023 -- this is real added steel (twinning), not a mere capacity relabel, so LengthKnown/Diameter being populated is correct per project convention. Four independent Egyptian sources (2 government, 2 media, spanning 2022-2024) converge on the same named project, corridor and purpose -- existence is high-confidence. CLASSIFICATION: national-grid gas transmission trunk (GASCO), correctly typed 'transmission', Fuel='Gas' -- both confirmed by the same sources (current ref verifies with Arabic terms 'تشغيل'/'التينة'/'168', not the literal English word 'operating', which is why the automated pre-check flagged it as a false negative). DUPLICATE check against the 30-row Egypt-gas-operating roster and the GulfPub list: P3366 'El Tina-Abu Sultan-New Administrative Capital' shares the El Tina origin but is a DIFFERENT physical pipe -- an EIB/GASCO EIA document (eib.org/files/pipeline/1162_Eltina_Abusultan_en.pdf) specifies the El Tina-Abu Sultan leg as 32-inch/60 km (vs this row's 42-inch/170 km to Mit Nema), i.e. two separate trunks radiating from the same El Tina hub to different destinations -- not a double-count. P3346 'El Noubareya Gas Pipeline' (El Noubareya->Al Qalyubia) also converges on the same Mit Nema/Qalyubia hub but originates from El Noubareya in the west, not El Tina -- a search hit ('استكمال تعديل مواسير الصرف المتعارضة مع خط غاز النوبارية - ميت نما') independently names a distinct 'Nubaria-Mit Nema' GASCO line, confirming Mit Nema is a real multi-line grid junction, not a single line entered twice under two names. GulfPub's Egypt gas roster has no entry matching 'El Tina' or 'Mit Nema' by name -- absence noted, not a red flag given the strength of the Egyptian-source corroboration. ATTRIBUTION: Owner1='Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Co' (EGAS) is defensible -- Oil & Gas Journal (ogj.com) confirms EGAS is the holding company that supervises/owns national gas transmission assets while GASCO (a subsidiary) 'was born in 1997 to manage, operate and maintain the national gas grid and its facilities.' The Operator field on the operators/owners tab (row 2506) is currently BLANK -- filled below with GASCO, which the Youm7 2-May-2022 article names explicitly as the implementer of this specific project.

validity.recommendation: SegmentCost looks understated/wrong. Recommend Update review and likely correct SegmentCost toward the ~EGP 4.0-4.5bn range that 2 independent sources report (or leave as an inferred range) rather than the current EGP 3,335,000,000.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM's current SegmentCost value is EGP 3,335,000,000 (no ref). Independent sourcing disagrees materially: Youm7 (2 May 2022, quoting the Petroleum Minister) and Egypt Oil & Gas (3 May 2022, English) both independently report the El-Tina/Mit Nema project cost as EGP 4.5 billion; Youm7 (14 Jan 2024) reports the 'duplication' phase completed 2023 at 'حوالي 4 مليار جنيه' (approximately EGP 4bn). Neither figure is close to GEM's 3.335bn (roughly 26% and 17% lower respectively). Could not find any source producing GEM's exact 3.335bn figure, so I am not proposing it as a verified ref -- recommend Update flag/correct this cell rather than staging a ref that would misrepresent the sourced range.

fills.researcher_notes: Youm7 2-May-2022 (quoting the Petroleum Minister) gives the exact value 'بطول 170 كم' for 'خط غاز التينة غرب / ميت نما'. Petroleum.gov.eg's Dec-2022 year-end report gives 168 km for the same-named line (minor as-built variance, same project). GEM's 170.00 matches the initial project announcement exactly.

Both sources explicitly name the line as running from El Tina (El Tina West / التينة غرب) to Mit Nema (ميت نما), matching sheet endpoints exactly. Mit Nema is a real, named village in Qalyub markaz, Al Qalyubia governorate.

Operator/Operator [ref] cells on the operators_owners tab (row 2506) are currently blank. Youm7 2-May-2022 headline itself is 'وزير البترول: جاسكو تنفذ 3 مشروعات...' (Petroleum Minister: GASCO implements 3 projects...) naming this exact project as GASCO's. OGJ corroborates GASCO's general role as the company that 'manages, operates and maintains the national gas grid and its facilities' under EGAS's supervisory ownership -- consistent with Owner1=EGAS / Operator=GASCO being distinct, correct roles, not a conflict.

Could not find any independent source documenting a specific delay event for this line. All located sources describe a fairly linear timeline (announced under implementation May 2022; base line reported complete by Dec 2022; a capacity-doubling twin pipe completed 2023) with no explicit schedule slip called out. Leaving Delay [ref] unresolved rather than fabricating a citation for the existing Delayed=yes/DelayType=confirmed value.

Not filling a ref for GEM's current EGP 3,335,000,000 value -- see validity concern above. Two independent sources put the cost at EGP 4.5bn (initial 2022 announcement) and ~EGP 4bn (2023 duplication-phase completion report); neither matches GEM's figure. Recommend Update correct the value rather than staging a ref that would misrepresent the sourced figures.

routes.corridor_desc: Sourced Egyptian government/media reporting consistently names the corridor as GASCO's 'El Tina West / Mit Nema' national-grid trunk, carrying East Mediterranean offshore gas (Zohr/Nooros-era) from the El Tina area east of Port Said generally south-southwest across the eastern Nile Delta (through Sharqia Governorate, unconfirmed exact alignment) into Al Qalyubia Governorate, terminating at Mit Nema village (Qalyub markaz) -- a documented multi-line GASCO grid junction (a separate 'El Noubareya-Mit Nema' line, matching GEM P3346, also ties in there from the west). No route GeoJSON, KMZ, or as-built alignment map was located; the corridor above is inferred only from named endpoints and purpose statements in press/ministry sources, not a surveyed centerline -- treat as a loose bound, not a precise route. The El Tina start coordinate given is the broader 'Tina Bay/Plain' locality (a documented geographic feature east of Port Said city); the exact GASCO facility footprint within that area is not independently pinned down.
routes.researcher_notes: End coordinate (Mit Nema village) is a specific, independently sourced named-place match to the sheet's EndLocation. Start coordinate is a defensible but looser proxy for the named 'El Tina' area (Tina Bay/Plain, a documented geographic feature east of Port Said) rather than a pinned facility. No intermediate waypoints could be sourced, so RouteAccuracy is not upgraded beyond medium -- this is a corridor suggestion for a human routes-repo pass, not a route replacement.

summary: El Tina Gas Pipeline (P3343) is real and correctly classified as a GASCO national-grid gas transmission trunk (El Tina West/Mit Nema line, ~168-170km/42in, East Mediterranean gas to Cairo/Delta), confirmed by 4 independent Egyptian government/media sources 2022-2024, and is NOT a duplicate of P3366 (El Tina-Abu Sultan, different diameter/length) or P3346 (same Mit Nema hub, different origin); filled blank Operator (GASCO) and Location refs, but flagged SegmentCost (EGP 3.335bn) as inconsistent with 2 independent sources reporting EGP 4-4.5bn, and left Delay/SegmentCost refs UNRESOLVED.
